title: 5e-review-3: review integration (review, drift, orient, MCP tools)
description:
## Parent

sutra/83 (5e PRD: health metrics + similarity system)

## What to review

Final review after slices 5e-8 through 5e-11 land. The full L4 + L6 system is operational.

Reviewer focus:
- Does sutra_review produce a coherent report? Read it end-to-end: constraints → conventions → health → shape changes → deltas. Is the flow useful?
- Is semantic diff (hrr_shape_change) producing actionable findings? Test on real diffs — do the "subtle structural change" flags make sense?
- Does convention drift detection fire appropriately? Check both FCA-based and HRR-based paths on real components.
- Is the orient briefing useful with health context? Does it help an agent understand the quality landscape before making changes?
- Does sutra_health give useful per-file and per-component views?
- function_hotspot and code_age_volatility: are the on-demand biomarkers reasonable on real code?

## Blocked by

- sutra/93 (5e-8)
- sutra/94 (5e-9)
- sutra/95 (5e-10)
- sutra/96 (5e-11)"

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — verdict: needs-attention

Three medium findings, all verified by Claude:

1. **Semantic diff reads working tree instead of reviewed head** (src/similarity/diff.rs:175-176) — `detect_shape_changes` reads the "new" side from the filesystem, not from the reviewed commit. For staged or commit-range diffs, `hrr_shape_changes` can report on unrelated content.

2. **Convention drift fires on insufficient history** (src/tools/review.rs:612-628 → src/health/drift.rs:108) — `record_and_detect_drift` inserts the current snapshot before `detect_convention_drift` queries it. With DRIFT_WINDOW=3, one of two "historical" slots is the just-inserted current value, so drift fires after 1 real prior data point instead of 2.

3. **Blame parser reuses stale timestamp for repeated commits** (src/git.rs:20-39) — Porcelain blame omits metadata on repeated commit headers. The parser doesn't cache author-time by commit hash, so repeated commits inherit the intervening commit's timestamp. Corrupts code_age_volatility calculations.

No constraint violations. Convention violations are visibility-related (pub(crate) vs private consts, pub vs non-pub fns) — project convention noise, not real issues.
